extraction_scope: Worker-6 final mechanism adjudication from local XML/PDF/figure captions. Claims are bounded to direct assays and structure-activity observations in the paper; no unsupported cell-wall pathway is asserted.

mechanism_claims.claim_text: Brevinin-1GHa produced concentration-dependent membrane permeabilization in the SYTOX Green assay, with strong S. aureus permeability at higher multiples of MIC, weaker E. coli permeability, and C. albicans disruption at 4x MIC.
mechanism_claims.limitations: The paper reports fluorescence/permeability trends and selected percentages in text; exact full numeric curves remain figure-level, so no additional point values were fabricated.

mechanism_claims.entity_scope: Brevinin-1GHa against Staphylococcus aureus, Escherichia coli, and Candida albicans
mechanism_claims.claim_text: Time-kill assays support rapid concentration-dependent killing at 1x, 2x, and 4x MIC, with no countable cells at earlier times as dose increased.
mechanism_claims.limitations: Killing kinetics are treated as activity/mechanistic context, not a distinct molecular target mechanism.

mechanism_claims.claim_text: Brevinin-1GHa inhibited biofilm formation and eradicated preformed biofilms for S. aureus, E. coli, and C. albicans with source-supported MBIC/MBEC values in Table 3.
mechanism_claims.limitations: Biofilm activity is recorded as a phenotypic antibiofilm endpoint, not a quorum-sensing or biofilm-pathway mechanism.

mechanism_claims.claim_text: Analogue comparison supports a bounded structure-activity conclusion: removing the Rana-box sharply reduced antimicrobial activity, while moving the Rana-box reduced hemolysis but also reduced antimicrobial potency.
mechanism_claims.limitations: The conclusion is comparative SAR, not proof of a unique molecular mechanism.
